clue.text: One leaves old king some fertile land

indicators.note: one thing leaving another means it walks out of the word, so the letter for one is dropped

parts.note: Richard is the name of several English kings
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A monarch of old has a single estate of good farmland slip from his holdings.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plot planted with fruit trees, a productive piece of land.

clue.text: Bring down books to entertain setter and solver?

indicators.note: a host entertains guests by taking them in, so the books hold the pronoun

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
the setter and the solver together are us

explanation.surface: Books are brought in to amuse the puzzle's maker and its solver, bringing someone down.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to remove or topple them from power.

clue.text: Kept appointment with fate coming to Arthur's Seat

parts.note: to come is to turn up as arranged
one's lot is one's fate

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a date with destiny on Arthur's Seat, the hill overlooking Edinburgh.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur's Seat is an Edinburgh hill; here it means King Arthur's court.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelot is the legendary castle and court of King Arthur, his seat of power.

clue.text: Quarrel caused when posh school fails to open

indicators.note: the school's name fails to open, losing its first letter

parts.note: Harrow is an expensive English boarding school

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out when an elite school does not open for term.
explanation.walkthrough: A quarrel looks like a row, but it is also a bolt for a crossbow.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is a short square-headed arrow shot from a crossbow.

clue.text: Heavy rain's appearance in low Cornish river and lake

definitions.note: read as 'heavy rain is', so the definition is the noun heavy rain

parts.note: down means low, as in spirits
the Fal is a river in Cornwall

explanation.surface: A deluge shows up in a low-lying Cornish river and a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A downfall is a heavy fall of rain or snow.

clue.text: Ace in flying saucer gets break

indicators.note: the ace's letter is placed inside the rearranged word
something flying is in motion and disordered, so the letters of saucer are rearranged

parts.note: an ace is the A in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A fighter ace aboard a UFO gets his lucky break.
explanation.definitionFit: A caesura is a pause in a line of verse, a break in its rhythm.

clue.text: Cells initially needing permission to divide?

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of cells is used

parts.note: first letter of cells
leave is permission, as in leave to appeal

explanation.surface: Biological cells need a go-ahead before they split.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave is to split apart, so it means to divide.

clue.text: Old forward is beginning to employ special knowledge

parts.note: ex means former
pert means cheeky or forward

indicators.note: the beginning of employ is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of employ

explanation.surface: A cheeky former partner is starting to use specialist know-how.
explanation.definitionFit: Expertise is skill or know-how in a particular field.

clue.text: Leading Tories being honourable?

parts.note: up means ahead or leading, as in a score
the Tories are the political right

explanation.surface: Conservatives ahead in the polls, and acting honourably?
explanation.definitionFit: An upright person is honest and morally sound, so the word suits honourable.

clue.text: Bengalese AM broadcast not good for ratings

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered, so the letters are rearranged
not means the good's letter is left out of the pool

explanation.surface: A Bengali morning radio show is poor for audience figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ratings' suggests audience figures, but naval ratings are sailors below officer rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Able seamen are naval ratings, the ordinary sailors of a ship's crew.

clue.text: Belt in earthy shade uniform should accommodate

indicators.note: the word for uniform should take in and house the colour, holding it inside

parts.note: uniform means the same throughout
brown is the colour of earth

explanation.surface: A soldier's belt in a khaki-brown shade ought to suit the uniform it goes with.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sam Browne is a military officer's belt with a diagonal shoulder strap.

clue.text: Liberal Irish record overturned reveals grave danger

indicators.note: turned over, so the whole string is read from the end back to the start

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: An upturned record by an Irish Liberal politician exposes a serious threat.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril is serious, immediate risk of harm.

clue.text: Colt back around western states taking time in principle

indicators.note: the reversed young horse goes around the letter for western, enclosing it
back means the word for colt is read backwards

parts.note: a colt is a young horse, a foal

indicators.note: the word for states takes in the period of time, holding it inside

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A young horse brought back to the western states, as a matter of principle.
explanation.definitionFit: The law of averages is the supposed principle that things even out over many trials.

clue.text: Floated south across country with duck departing marshes

indicators.note: the swimming and south letters stretch across the country, enclosing it

parts.note: swam is to have floated in water

indicators.note: the duck departs, so its letter is removed

parts.note: Poland is a country
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: Someone swam south across a country once the duck had gone, reaching the wetlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Swamplands are tracts of waterlogged ground, the same as marshes.

clue.text: Refused husband the covers: furious about that?

indicators.note: the word for furious goes round everything else

parts.note: wild means furious

indicators.note: the word 'the' covers the husband's letter, wrapping it

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy

explanation.surface: A wife refuses her husband the bedclothes, and he is livid about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a row over the duvet; 'the covers' is not bedding but an instruction for 'the' to wrap H.
explanation.definitionFit: To withhold something is to refuse to give it, so withheld means refused.

clue.text: Pulse right to coat in warm batter

indicators.note: the warm word coats the right, wrapping round it

parts.note: to heat is to warm
to beat is to batter

explanation.surface: The proper way to dip food in warm batter, as the cook's heart races.
explanation.walkthrough: Batter looks like the cooking mixture but is the verb, to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A heartbeat is a single pulse of the heart.

clue.text: Ceremonial instruments used in Lysistrata

indicators.note: the answer is a run of letters used inside the play's title

parts.note: the letters sit in the middle of the title, after Ly and before ta

explanation.surface: Ritual rattles were part of a production of Aristophanes' comedy Lysistrata.
explanation.definitionFit: Sistra are metal rattles shaken in ancient Egyptian religious rites, plural of sistrum.

clue.text: Cologne is this loud with student festivity and shouting?

parts.note: a rag is a British student charity festival
a rant is a loud tirade

explanation.surface: Is the German city of Cologne loud with student parties and yelling?
explanation.walkthrough: Cologne looks like the German city but is eau de cologne, the scent. F is forte, loud in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Cologne is a perfumed toilet water, so it is sweet-smelling.

clue.text: Placing financial restriction on ordinary folk is old hat

indicators.note: the restriction is placed on the folk, coming after them in the answer

parts.note: the mob is the common people
a cap is a limit, such as on spending

explanation.surface: A spending cap on the common people is a tired, old-fashioned idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' looks like an idiom for stale, but here it is literal: a hat from the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobcap is a soft frilled cap worn indoors by women in the 18th and 19th centuries.

clue.text: Start to grasp socially acceptable English dance

indicators.note: the start word grasps the letter for socially acceptable, holding it inside

parts.note: to begin is to start
U means upper-class or socially acceptable, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: Beginning to pick up a respectable English dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The beguine is a Caribbean ballroom dance similar to the rumba.

clue.text: Horrible to leave note without regrets?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the leaving and note go outside the regrets

parts.note: to go is to leave
rues means regrets
me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: It is a dreadful thing to walk out leaving only a note and no remorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome means causing horror or disgust, so it is a synonym of horrible.

clue.text: Reference work one on China so complex?

definitions.note: an adjective: having a complex of this kind

parts.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
one is the Roman numeral I
china is rhyming slang for mate: china plate, so pal

explanation.surface: Is a reference book with one entry on China really so complicated?
explanation.walkthrough: Complex looks like 'complicated' but is the noun of psychology, the Oedipus complex.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedipal describes the Oedipus complex, Freud's term for a child's attraction to the opposite-sex parent.

clue.text: Failure at table to avoid row becoming audible

indicators.note: heard aloud rather than read, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: to miss is to avoid and a queue is a row, so 'miss queue'

explanation.surface: A dinner-table blunder: avoiding an argument that turns into a shouting match.
explanation.walkthrough: Table looks like a dining table, but it is a billiards or snooker table; row is a line, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscue is a faulty stroke in billiards or snooker where the cue slips off the ball.

clue.text: Trifle with edging hotel prepared like dip

indicators.note: prepared as a dish is made up, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trifle, given a border at the hotel, is made like a dip for the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture makes 'dip' a sauce, but in slang a dip is a pickpocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A light-fingered person steals deftly, which is exactly what a pickpocket does.

clue.text: River near tree bordering area in field

indicators.note: the river is near the rest, placed directly before it
the tree borders the area, enclosing its letter

parts.note: the elm is a tree

explanation.surface: A river runs by a tree at the edge of a patch in a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a field or domain of activity, as in the realm of science.

clue.text: Stick close to flatmate in block

indicators.note: the last letter is put in the block word

parts.note: to bar is to block

indicators.note: the close of flatmate is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of flatmate

explanation.surface: Staying near a flatmate in the same apartment block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick close' reads as a phrase, but Stick alone is the definition, meaning endure.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick or bear something is to tolerate or put up with it.

clue.text: Blocking passage in church, one wet behind ears

indicators.note: one blocks the passage by standing in it, placed inside the word

parts.note: the nave is the main central space of a church, leading to the altar
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone green and inexperienced stands in the church aisle, in everyone's way.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet behind the ears is an idiom for inexperienced or innocent, the same as naive.

clue.text: Curmudgeon spotted with daughter out for fruit

parts.note: a crab is a grumpy, crabby person

indicators.note: the daughter is out, so her letter is removed

parts.note: dapple means marked with spots

explanation.surface: A grouch is spotted with his daughter, heading out for some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A crab apple is a small, sour wild apple, a type of fruit.

clue.text: Odd characters in secret exercises on the staff

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of secret, first, third and fifth, are taken

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of secret
PT is physical training, i.e. exercises
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Secret exercises are being done by members of the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The staff' reads as employees, but here a staff is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptre is an ornamental rod carried by a monarch, a ceremonial staff.

clue.text: Barrister and casual worker having endless fun

parts.note: a temp is a temporary employee

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a lark is a bit of fun

explanation.surface: A lawyer and a temp having nonstop fun together.
explanation.definitionFit: A Templar is a barrister or law student with chambers in the Temple, the legal district of London.
